l: peace, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The Lamanites who believe the truth bury their weapons of war for peace. Their refusal to fight and their willingness to suffer rather than commit sin demonstrate their commitment to peace.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: The Lamanites swear vengeance against the Nephites, destroy the people in the land of Ammonihah, and later return to their own land after being driven and slain in battles. Many Lamanites remember the words preached by Aaron and his brethren, believe in the Lord, and join the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi, while rulers from the remnant of the children of Amulon cause believers to be put to death by fire. The seed of Amulon and his brethren are hunted, scattered, and slain, fulfilling the words of Abinadi. The converted Lamanites bury their weapons of war, become a righteous people, keep the law of Moses, and look forward to the coming of Christ through faith.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: The Lamanites swear vengeance upon the Nephites, destroy the people in the land of Ammonihah, and have many battles with the Nephites in which they are driven and slain. Many Lamanites later believe in the Lord, join the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi, bury their weapons of war, and become a righteous people.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: The Nephites drive and slay the Lamanites in many battles and slay almost all the seed of Amulon and his brethren who are among the Lamanites.

l: people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi are not slain by the Lamanites at that time. Many Lamanites join themselves to them and become part of the people of God.

l: seed of Amulon and his brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: Almost all the seed of Amulon and his brethren are slain by the Nephites. The remnant causes many Lamanites who believe to be put to death by fire, and the seed are later hunted, scattered, and slain by the Lamanites.

l: Aaron, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: Aaron and his brethren preach to the Lamanites, and many later remember their words, believe in the Lord, and are converted in the wilderness.

l: Abinadi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: Abinadi is identified as the first to suffer death by fire because of his belief in God. His words concerning the seed of the priests who caused his death are fulfilled when they are hunted, scattered, and slain.

l: weapons of war, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: The Lamanites who join the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi bury their weapons of war according as their brethren had.

l: battles, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: The Lamanites have many battles with the Nephites and are driven and slain. When the Lamanites cannot overpower the Nephites, they return again to their own land.

l: destruction of the people of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: The Lamanites go into the borders of the land of Zarahemla, fall upon the people in the land of Ammonihah, and destroy them.

l: martyrdom of the believers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: The rulers who are the remnant of the children of Amulon cause all those who believe in the Lord and his power to be put to death. This martyrdom stirs many of their brethren to anger and begins contention in the wilderness.

l: death by fire, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: Many believers among the Lamanites suffer death by fire because of their belief. This fulfills the meaning of Abinadi's statement about what would happen to him and his seed.

l: conversion of the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: After suffering much loss and many afflictions, many Lamanites remember the words preached by Aaron and his brethren, disbelieve the traditions of their fathers, believe in the Lord, and are converted in the wilderness.

l: burial of weapons of war, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: The Lamanites who join the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi bury their weapons of war and begin to be a righteous people.

l: Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: Many Lamanites believe in the Lord and that he gives great power unto the Nephites. The Lord grants unto Ammon, Aaron, Omner, Himni, and their brethren according to their prayers and verifies his word unto them.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: Abinadi suffers death by fire because of his belief in God. The people who join the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi are called the people of God.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: The Lamanites who keep the law of Moses look forward to the coming of Christ and believe that the law of Moses is a type of his coming.

l: law of Moses, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: The converted Lamanites keep the law of Moses because it is not all fulfilled. They do not suppose that salvation comes by the law of Moses, but it strengthens their faith in Christ until he is revealed.

l: coming of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: The converted Lamanites look forward to the coming of Christ and consider the law of Moses to be a type of his coming.

l: faith in Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: The law of Moses serves to strengthen the Lamanites' faith in Christ. Through faith and the spirit of prophecy, they retain a hope unto eternal salvation.

l: words of Abinadi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 25
s: The words of Abinadi concerning the seed of the priests who caused him to suffer death by fire are brought to pass when their seed are hunted, scattered, and slain.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: Ammon rejoices with his brethren over the blessings God granted through their journey from Zarahemla to Nephi and their preaching among the Lamanites. He explains that many Lamanites were brought from darkness into God's light, converted, and gathered into God's fold. Ammon recounts the afflictions he and his brethren endured and credits God’s power, mercy, and word for their success. He teaches that repentance, faith, good works, and continual prayer bring knowledge of God’s mysteries and lead to salvation.

l: Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: Ammon rejoices in God for enabling him and his brethren to help bring many Lamanites to repentance. He rejects boasting in his own strength and instead boasts in God, declaring that he is weak and that God’s power enables him to do all things.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: God grants blessings, comforts Ammon and his brethren, gives them success, and delivers them from imprisonment and affliction. He brings repentant people from darkness, death, and misery into light, salvation, and his fold.

l: Ammon’s brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: Ammon's brethren labor with him among the Lamanites, enduring travel, privation, rejection, mocking, violence, imprisonment, and other afflictions. They rejoice because many people have been brought to repentance through their work.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: The Lamanites were described as being in darkness and under traditions that led many into iniquity and violence. Many were taught by Ammon and his brethren, brought to repentance, and changed so that they buried their weapons and preferred to sacrifice their own lives rather than kill their enemies.

l: more than a thousand converts, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: The Lamanite converts were brought into the fold of God and into his everlasting light and salvation. They showed sincerity through love for their brethren, willingness to sacrifice their lives, and hatred of sin.

l: land of Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: The land of Zarahemla was the place from which Ammon and his brethren departed. Its people had doubted that the Lamanites could be brought to the knowledge of the truth and had considered taking up arms against them.

l: land of Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: The land of Nephi was the destination where Ammon and his brethren went to preach to the Lamanites. They taught there in houses, streets, hills, temples, and synagogues.

l: journey from Zarahemla to Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: The journey from Zarahemla to Nephi was undertaken to preach to the Lamanites rather than to destroy them. During it, Ammon and his brethren endured privation and affliction and relied on the mercies of God.

l: teaching among the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: Preaching to the Lamanites involved teaching in their homes, streets, hills, temples, and synagogues. Ammon and his brethren were often cast out, mocked, beaten, stoned, bound, and imprisoned, but God delivered them.

l: conversion of the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: The conversion of the Lamanites brought thousands from darkness and the pains of hell into God's light, salvation, and fold. The converts demonstrated their change through love for their brethren and rejection of violence and sin.

l: gospel of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: The gospel of God is associated with the power of God's word that brought the Lamanites to repentance and caused them to sing redeeming love. Through it, people could learn the mysteries of God and receive salvation.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: Repentance is required for people to know the mysteries of God and receive salvation. Through repentance, many Lamanites were brought out of darkness and released from the pains of hell.

l: faith in Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: Faith, together with repentance, good works, and continual prayer, is described as a way to receive knowledge of God's mysteries. Those who exercise faith can help bring thousands of souls to repentance.

l: salvation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: Salvation is given as God brings people from death, misery, darkness, and destruction into everlasting light. It is promised to those who repent and believe on God's name.

l: sin, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: Sin is associated with the Lamanites' former violence and iniquity and with Ammon and his brethren's earlier rebellion against God's church. The converts showed their change by developing hatred toward sin.

l: love, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: Love for their brethren led many Lamanites to bury their weapons and prefer death over killing an enemy. Love also became evidence of the converts' sincerity.

l: mercy, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: God's mercy spared Ammon and his brethren from the justice they deserved and brought them across the gulf of death and misery. His mercies extend over all the earth and are available to those who repent.

l: afflictions, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: Ammon and his brethren endured travel, privation, rejection, mocking, spitting, beatings, stoning, binding, imprisonment, and other afflictions while preaching. They bore these sufferings patiently in hopes of saving souls.

l: joy, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: Ammon's joy is full because many Lamanites have been brought to repentance and into God's fold. He says his joy carries him to boast in God and gives him reason to praise and thank God forever.

l: miraculous power of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: God's power enabled Ammon and his brethren to perform mighty miracles, endure their work, and escape imprisonment. Through the power of God's word in them, many Lamanites were released from the pains of hell and brought to repentance.

l: instruments in God's hands, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 26
s: Ammon and his brethren were instruments in God's hands in bringing the Lamanites into God's light and fold. They attribute the great and marvelous work to God rather than to their own strength or wisdom.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The Lamanites returned to the land of Nephi after failing to destroy the Nephites, while the Amalekites stirred them to attack the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi. Ammon and his brethren led the people to seek refuge among the Nephites, and the Lord directed them to leave the land. The Nephites granted them the land of Jershon, protected them with armies, and called them the people of Ammon. The people of Ammon were known for their repentance, faith in Christ, honesty, zeal, and refusal to take up arms against their brethren.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The Lamanites returned to the land of Nephi after failing to destroy the Nephites. The Amalekites stirred them to anger against the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi, and they began again to destroy them.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The Nephites were the people to whom the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi sought refuge. They gave them the land of Jershon, placed armies between them and the land of Nephi, and protected them.

l: land of Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The land of Nephi was where the Lamanites returned after their failed war against the Nephites. The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi departed from it because the Lord commanded them to leave.

l: Amalekites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The Amalekites were exceedingly angry because of their losses. They stirred up the Lamanites against the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi and began again to destroy them.

l: people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi refused to take up arms and suffered themselves to be slain. At the Lord’s command, they left the land of Nephi, received the land of Jershon as an inheritance, and were thereafter called the people of Ammon.

l: Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: Ammon asked the king to let the people flee to the Nephites and inquired of the Lord on their behalf. He led them toward the land of Zarahemla, met Alma, and helped bring the people to the land of Jershon.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: Alma met Ammon and his brethren in the wilderness, and the meeting was joyful. He conducted them to the land of Zarahemla and related his conversion to the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi.

l: Anti-Nephi-Lehi (king), The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The king feared that the Nephites would destroy his people because of their murders and sins. He agreed to go to the Nephites if the Lord commanded it and promised that the people would otherwise perish in the land.

l: chief judge, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The chief judge received Alma and his brethren and heard what had happened among the Lamanites. He sent a proclamation throughout the land seeking the people’s voice concerning admitting the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi.

l: Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The Lord commanded Ammon to get the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi out of the land so they would not perish. He said that Satan had great hold on the hearts of the Amalekites and promised to preserve the people in that generation.

l: land of Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The land of Zarahemla was the destination sought by the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi. Ammon and his brethren went toward it, and Alma conducted them there before they settled in the land of Jershon.

l: land of Jershon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The land of Jershon was given by the Nephites to the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi for an inheritance. It was on the east by the sea and joined the land Bountiful.

l: people of Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi were called the people of Ammon after taking possession of the land of Jershon. They were distinguished for zeal toward God and men, honesty, uprightness, and firm faith in Christ.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The people of Ammon had hope and views of Christ and the resurrection. They regarded Christ’s victory over death as swallowing up death for them.

l: destruction, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The Amalekites and Lamanites brought destruction upon the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi. Ammon and his brethren were moved with compassion when they saw this destruction.

l: murder, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi had committed many murders before their repentance. They abhorred shedding the blood of their brethren and would suffer death rather than commit further murder.

l: sin, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi feared taking up arms because they might commit sin. Their former sins and murders led them to seek refuge among the Nephites.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi experienced sore repentance because of their many murders and awful wickedness. Their repentance contributed to their great fear of taking up arms against their brethren.

l: inheritance lands in Jershon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The Nephites gave the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi the land of Jershon for an inheritance. The people went down into the land and took possession of it.

l: armies, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The Nephites placed their armies between the land of Jershon and the land of Nephi to protect the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi. The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi were to give a portion of their substance to help maintain the armies.

l: conversion of Alma, Ammon, Aaron, Omner, and Himni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: Alma related his conversion, together with the conversion of Ammon, Aaron, Omner, and Himni, to the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi. His account caused great joy among them.

l: faith of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The people of Ammon were firm in the faith of Christ even unto the end. Their faith gave them hope concerning death and the resurrection.

l: death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The people of Ammon did not view death with terror because of their hope and views of Christ and the resurrection. They would suffer death in the most aggravating and distressing manner rather than take up the sword or cimeter against their brethren.

l: resurrection of the dead, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The people of Ammon hoped in Christ and the resurrection. Because of this hope, death was swallowed up to them by the victory of Christ over it.

l: victory of Christ over death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 27
s: The people of Ammon believed that Christ’s victory over death swallowed up death for them. This belief helped them refuse to fight against their brethren even when facing death.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: After the people of Ammon and a church were established in the land of Jershon, the Lamanites followed their brethren into the wilderness and fought the Nephites in a tremendous battle. The Lamanites were slain, driven, and scattered, while the Nephites also suffered a great slaughter and returned to their land. The fifteenth year of the reign of the judges ended with widespread mourning, fasting, and prayer, as many thousands had died and their kindred mourned. The unit teaches that sin, transgression, and the power of the devil bring destruction and sorrow, while the light of Christ brings hope, joy, and rejoicing.

l: people of Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: The people of Ammon were established in the land of Jershon, where they were received and kept safe.

l: land of Jershon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: The land of Jershon became the place where the people of Ammon and a church were established. The armies of the Nephites were set round about it.

l: armies of the Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: The armies of the Nephites were set round about the land of Jershon and in all the borders around the land of Zarahemla. They fought the Lamanites and drove and scattered them.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: The Nephites suffered a tremendous slaughter, but they drove and scattered the Lamanites and returned to their land. Many Nephites mourned kindred who had been slain.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: The Lamanites followed their brethren into the wilderness, suffered great losses, and were driven and scattered by the Nephites.

l: battle, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: A tremendous battle occurred between the Nephites and the Lamanites, unlike any previously known among the people in the land since Lehi left Jerusalem.

l: mourning and lamentation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: Mourning and lamentation were heard throughout the land among the people of Nephi. Widows, fathers, daughters, and brothers mourned for kindred who had been slain.

l: reign of the judges, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: The fifteenth year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi ended after years of wars, contentions, and the destruction of many thousands of lives.

l: Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: Ammon is included in the account of the journeyings, sufferings, sorrows, afflictions, joy, and safety of the brethren in the land of Jershon.

l: Ammon’s brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: Ammon’s brethren are described as journeying in the land of Nephi, suffering and experiencing sorrow, affliction, incomprehensible joy, and reception and safety in the land of Jershon.

l: land of Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: The account describes the journeyings and sufferings of Ammon and his brethren in the land of Nephi.

l: Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: The Lord is identified as the source of promises concerning the fate of the dead. The text asks the Lord, the Redeemer of all men, to bless the souls of Ammon and his brethren forever.

l: war, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: Wars and contentions occurred among the Nephites, as well as wars between the Nephites and the Lamanites, from the first year through the fifteenth year of the reign of the judges.

l: destruction, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: The wars brought about the destruction of many thousands of lives and an awful scene of bloodshed.

l: bloodshed, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: The period from the first year to the fifteenth year of the reign of the judges brought about extensive bloodshed, with many thousands slain.

l: inequality of man, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: The different responses to the loss of kindred show how great the inequality of man is because of sin and transgression and the power of the devil.

l: wickedness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: Sin and transgression are identified as causes of the inequality of man and the sorrow associated with death and destruction.

l: devil, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: The devil brings the power that contributes to the inequality of man through cunning plans designed to ensnare the hearts of men.

l: sorrow, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: Sorrow comes from death and destruction among men and from the loss of kindred. The text also describes sorrowful days, solemnity, fasting, and prayer.

l: rejoicing, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: Some mourners rejoice and exult because they have hope and knowledge, according to the promises of the Lord, that their kindred are raised to dwell at the right hand of God in never-ending happiness.

l: light of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: The light of Christ brings life and is identified as the reason for joy amid death and destruction.

l: death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 28
s: Death and destruction caused many thousands to be slain and led their kindred to mourn. The dead are described either as consigned to endless wo or as raised to dwell at the right hand of God in never-ending happiness.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The speaker wishes to declare repentance and the plan of redemption to every people but recognizes that he should be content with the work allotted to him. He teaches that God grants people according to their desires and gives nations His word in wisdom. The speaker glories in being an instrument in the hands of God, rejoices in the repentance of others, and remembers that God delivered his fathers from captivity and bondage. He also rejoices in the success of his brethren who went to the land of Nephi and prays that they and the fruit of their labors may enter the kingdom of God.

l: Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The Lord allots work and grants people according to their desires. He gives nations His word in their own nation and tongue, calls the speaker by a holy calling, hears prayer, extends a merciful arm, and delivers people from bondage.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: God is described as just, wise, and true. The speaker desires to be an instrument in His hands, remembers His deliverance of the fathers, and asks that His will be done.

l: Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The speaker wishes he were an angel so he could proclaim repentance to every people, but recognizes that he should be content with his allotted work. He glories in what the Lord has commanded, rejoices in the repentance and success of others, and remembers the Lord’s mercy toward him.

l: Ammon’s brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The speaker rejoices in the success of his brethren who went to the land of Nephi. They labored exceedingly and brought forth much fruit.

l: this people, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The speaker has been called to preach the word unto this people and has received much success in doing so.

l: the fathers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The fathers were held in captivity and were delivered from bondage by the Lord, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

l: land of Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The brethren went up to the land of Nephi, where they labored exceedingly and brought forth much fruit.

l: kingdom of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The speaker asks God to grant that his brethren and those who are the fruit of their labors may sit down in the kingdom of God and praise Him forever.

l: church, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The Lord established His church among the fathers after delivering them from bondage.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The speaker wishes to cry repentance unto every people and declare it with the plan of redemption. He rejoices when many of his brethren become truly penitent and come unto the Lord.

l: the plan of redemption, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The speaker wants to declare the plan of redemption to every soul so that people will repent and come unto God.

l: word of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The Lord gives His word to all nations in their own nation and tongue, and the speaker has been called to preach the word unto this people.

l: evil, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: Good and evil have come before all people. Those who know neither are blameless, while those who know both receive according to their desires.

l: joy, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The speaker’s joy comes from being an instrument in God’s hands, seeing people repent, and witnessing the success of his brethren. His joy becomes so great that his soul is carried away as it were from the body.

l: prayer, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The speaker remembers that the Lord heard his prayer.

l: captivity, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The speaker remembers the captivity of his fathers and knows that the Lord delivered them from it.

l: bondage, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The Lord delivered the fathers out of bondage and established His church among them.

l: holy calling, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The Lord called the speaker by a holy calling to preach the word unto this people.

l: teaching among the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The speaker believes he should be content to perform the work to which he has been called.

l: success, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The speaker has received much success in preaching, and he rejoices even more in the success of his brethren who went to the land of Nephi.

l: the fruit of their labors, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The fruit of the brethren’s labors consists of those who may enter the kingdom of God and praise Him forever.

l: the merciful arm, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 29
s: The speaker remembers the Lord’s merciful arm, which the Lord extended toward him.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: After the people of Ammon were established in the land of Jershon and the Lamanites were driven out, continual peace prevailed among the Nephites while the people observed the commandments and the law of Moses. In the latter end of the seventeenth year, Korihor, an Anti-Christ, preached against the prophecies of the prophets and denied Christ, God, and the atonement, leading many into wickedness. Alma confronted Korihor, who demanded a sign, and God struck him dumb; Korihor then confessed that the devil had deceived him. Korihor was cast out, later trodden down and killed among the Zoramites, and the people were convinced of his wickedness and returned to the Lord.

l: people of Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: The people of Ammon were established in the land of Jershon. They took Korihor, bound him, and carried him before Ammon, who caused him to be carried out of the land.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: The Lamanites were driven out of the land, and their dead were buried by the people of the land.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: The Nephites experienced continual peace after the dead were buried and the people fasted, mourned, and prayed. Their dead were not numbered because of the greatness of their numbers.

l: land of Jershon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: The land of Jershon became the place where the people of Ammon were established after the Lamanites were driven out. Korihor preached there but was taken and carried before Ammon.

l: land of Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: Korihor came into the land of Zarahemla and preached against the prophecies concerning the coming of Christ. He was later sent there to be brought before Alma and the chief judge.

l: land of Gideon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: Korihor went to the land of Gideon and preached against Christ and the prophecies. He had little success there and was taken, bound, and carried before the high priest and chief judge.

l: peace, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: Continual peace began throughout all the land in the sixteenth year of the reign of the judges and continued into the commencement of the seventeenth year.

l: law of Moses, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: The people strictly observed the ordinances of God according to the law of Moses. They were taught to keep the law of Moses until it should be fulfilled.

l: Anti-Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: An Anti-Christ came into the land and preached against the prophecies concerning the coming of Christ. Korihor was identified as an Anti-Christ.

l: Korihor, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: Korihor preached that there should be no Christ, that there was no God, and that there could be no atonement, leading many into wickedness. After demanding a sign from Alma, he was struck dumb, confessed that the devil had deceived him, was cast out, and later died after being trodden down among the Zoramites.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: Korihor preached against the prophecies concerning the coming of Christ and denied that Christ would come or be slain for the sins of the world. Alma testified that Christ would come.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: Alma testified that there is a God and said that the earth, its motion, and the planets witness of a Supreme Creator. God struck Korihor dumb after Korihor demanded a sign.

l: devil, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: The devil was said to have power over Korihor and to carry him about while working devices to destroy the children of God. Korihor later confessed that the devil appeared to him as an angel and taught him what to say.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: Alma told Korihor that he and his brethren did not receive gain for their labors in the church and that he had labored with his own hands for support. Alma warned Korihor that God would strike him dumb, and Korihor was struck dumb according to Alma's words.

l: Zoramites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: The Zoramites were a people who had separated themselves from the Nephites and were led by Zoram. Korihor was among them when he was run upon and trodden down until he was dead.

l: prophets, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: The prophets had spoken prophecies concerning the coming of Christ. Korihor preached against those prophecies, calling them foolish traditions.

l: prophecies, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: The prophecies concerned the coming of Christ and were described by Korihor as foolish traditions. Alma defended them and testified that Christ would come.

l: the Atonement of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: Korihor taught that there could be no atonement made for the sins of men. He instead taught that every man fared according to the management of the creature.

l: sign, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: Korihor demanded a sign to convince him that there was a God. Alma gave him a sign by declaring that he would be struck dumb.

l: curse, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: Korihor recognized that his dumbness was a curse brought upon him after he withstood the truth. Alma refused to ask that the curse be taken away because Korihor would again lead away the hearts of the people.

l: Korihor's dumbness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: Korihor was struck dumb and could not speak after Alma's declaration. He wrote that only the power of God could have caused it and later remained dumb after being cast out.

l: Korihor's death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: Korihor was run upon and trodden down among the Zoramites until he was dead. His death was presented as the end of one who perverted the ways of the Lord.

l: law against belief, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 30
s: There was no law against a man's belief because such a law would be contrary to the commands of God and would bring men onto unequal grounds. People were punished for crimes such as murder, robbery, theft, and adultery, but not for belief.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: Alma learned that the Zoramites were perverting the ways of God and feared that they would ally with the Lamanites. He and Ammon, Aaron, Omner, Amulek, Zeezrom, Shiblon, and Corianton went among the Zoramites to preach the word of God. The Zoramites worshipped at the Rameumptom, prayed that they were chosen, rejected the tradition of belief in Christ, and set their hearts on riches and pride. Alma prayed for strength, comfort, wisdom, and success, and after he blessed his companions they were filled with the Holy Spirit and strengthened to labor among the people.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: Alma became sorrowful when he learned of the Zoramites' iniquity and separation from the Nephites. He went with companions to preach among them, was grieved by their worship and pride, and prayed for strength, comfort, wisdom, and success.

l: Zoramites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: The Zoramites were dissenters from the Nephites who had fallen into great errors and perverted the ways of the Lord. They worshipped at the Rameumptom, believed they were chosen, rejected belief in Christ, and set their hearts on riches and pride.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: The Nephites feared that the Zoramites would enter into correspondence with the Lamanites and cause great loss.

l: Antionum, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: Antionum was the land where the Zoramites had gathered. It lay east of Zarahemla, near the seashore, south of Jershon, and bordered the wilderness full of Lamanites.

l: Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: Ammon went with Alma, Aaron, Omner, Amulek, Zeezrom, Shiblon, and Corianton among the Zoramites to preach the word. Alma prayed that Ammon would be comforted and strengthened in Christ.

l: Aaron, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: Aaron went with Alma and the others among the Zoramites to preach the word. Alma prayed that Aaron would be comforted and strengthened in Christ.

l: Omner, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: Omner went with Alma and the others among the Zoramites to preach the word. Alma prayed that Omner would be comforted and strengthened in Christ.

l: Amulek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: Amulek went with Alma among the Zoramites to preach the word. Alma prayed that Amulek would be comforted and strengthened in Christ.

l: Zeezrom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: Zeezrom went with Alma among the Zoramites to preach the word. Alma prayed that Zeezrom would be comforted and strengthened in Christ.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: God was addressed in the Zoramites' repeated prayer of thanks and in Alma's petitions for strength, comfort, wisdom, and success. Alma asked God to help bring the Zoramites again unto Him in Christ.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: The Zoramites said they believed there would be no Christ and rejected the tradition that led their brethren to believe in Him. Alma asked God to comfort the souls of his companions in Christ and to bring the Zoramites again unto God in Christ.

l: Rameumptom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: Rameumptom was the name the Zoramites gave to the high place in the center of their synagogues where they stood to offer their prayer.

l: synagogues, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: The Zoramites had built synagogues and gathered in them on one day of the week called the day of the Lord. Their synagogues contained a high place for standing and praying.

l: prayer, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: The Zoramites offered the same prayer at the holy stand, thanking God that they were chosen and separated from their brethren, then did not speak of God again until the next gathering. Alma used prayer to seek strength, comfort, wisdom, and success for his work among them.

l: word of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: The word of God had a powerful effect on the minds of the people and was judged worth trying among the Zoramites. Alma and his companions went into the land to preach it.

l: the Spirit of the Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: The Holy Spirit filled Alma's companions after Alma clapped his hands upon them. They then separated to labor without taking thought for their food, drink, or clothing.

l: preaching of the word, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: Preaching of the word had a greater tendency to lead the people to do what was just than the sword or anything else that had happened to them. Alma therefore chose to use it among the Zoramites.

l: separation of the Zoramites from the Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: The separation of the Zoramites from the Nephites caused Alma great sorrow. The Nephites feared that this separation would lead the Zoramites to correspond with the Lamanites.

l: worship at the holy stand, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: Worship at the holy stand required each Zoramite to stand on a raised place, stretch forth the hands toward heaven, and offer the same prayer. Afterward, they returned home and did not speak of God again until the next gathering.

l: coming of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: The Zoramites believed that there would be no Christ and said that their brethren were bound by a belief in things to come that they knew nothing about.

l: wickedness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: Alma was sorrowful because of the iniquity among the Zoramites and saw them as a wicked and perverse people. He asked God to help him bear the afflictions caused by their iniquity.

l: pride, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: The Zoramites' hearts were lifted up in great boasting and pride. They cried to God with their mouths while being puffed up by the vain things of the world.

l: riches, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: The Zoramites' hearts were set upon gold, silver, costly apparel, ringlets, bracelets, ornaments of gold, and other precious things. Their desire for these fine goods accompanied their boasting and worship.

l: Alma's prayer, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 31
s: In Alma's prayer, he asked God for strength to bear the Zoramites' wickedness, comfort in Christ, success for himself and his fellow laborers, and power and wisdom to bring the Zoramites again unto God. Afterward, his companions were filled with the Holy Spirit and were strengthened to endure their afflictions.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: Alma teaches the poor in heart, who have been cast out of the synagogues because of their poverty, that God can be worshiped anywhere and that humility can lead to repentance and salvation. He explains that faith is hope in things not seen and that knowledge comes through an experiment upon the word. Alma compares the word to a seed that grows into a tree when nourished by faith, diligence, patience, and care. The tree yields precious fruit and springs up unto everlasting life.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: Alma teaches the poor in heart on the hill Onidah. He explains humility, repentance, faith, knowledge, and the growth of the word through the comparisons of a seed and a tree.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: God may be worshiped outside synagogues, and He is merciful unto all who believe on His name. He imparts His word by angels unto men and women, and words are also given to little children.

l: poor class of people, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: The poor class of people begin to have success after much labor among them. They have been cast out of the synagogues because of the coarseness of their apparel and their poverty.

l: the poor in heart, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: The poor in heart come to Alma because they are despised, cast out of their synagogues, and without a place to worship. Their afflictions have humbled them and prepared them to hear the word.

l: synagogues, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: The synagogues are places where the people seek to worship God. The poor are cast out of them because of their apparel and poverty.

l: word of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: The word of God is believed, experimented upon, nourished, and compared to a seed. It can enlarge the soul, enlighten understanding, expand the mind, and lead to everlasting life.

l: worship of the Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: Worship of God is not limited to synagogues or to once a week. The poor are taught that they can worship God despite being cast out.

l: poverty, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: Poverty causes the people to be despised by their brethren and priests and to be cast out of the synagogues. Their poverty brings some of them to a lowliness of heart.

l: affliction, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: The afflictions of the poor have truly humbled them and placed them in a preparation to hear the word.

l: humility, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: Those who are lowly in heart are blessed. Being compelled to be humble can lead a person to seek repentance, while those who humble themselves without compulsion are more blessed.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: Whoever repents shall find mercy, and whoever finds mercy and endures to the end shall be saved.

l: faith in Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: Faith is not a perfect knowledge of things but hope for things that are not seen and are true. Faith is exercised by giving place to the word and nourishing it with diligence, patience, and care.

l: knowledge, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: Knowledge is distinguished from faith because a person who knows a thing has no cause to believe it. Knowledge becomes perfect in a particular matter when the word has enlarged the soul and enlightened the understanding, though faith is not thereby to be laid aside.

l: experiment upon the word, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: An experiment upon the word begins when a person awakens and exercises even a particle of faith or a desire to believe. The person gives place for the word, observes whether it swells and grows, and learns whether the seed is good.

l: seed (Alma's listeners' seed), The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: The word is compared to a seed planted in the heart. A good seed swells, sprouts, grows, enlarges the soul, enlightens understanding, and strengthens faith; if it is neglected or resisted, it does not grow.

l: tree (the planted word), The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: The growing seed becomes a tree that must be nourished with great care, faith, diligence, and patience. If neglected, it lacks root, withers in the heat, and is cast out; if nourished, it brings forth fruit.

l: tree of life, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: The fruit of the tree of life cannot be plucked if the word is not nourished while looking forward with an eye of faith.

l: fruit, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: The fruit comes from nourishing the tree with faith, diligence, patience, and long-suffering. It is most precious, sweet above all that is sweet, white above all that is white, and pure above all that is pure.

l: everlasting life, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: A tree nourished by faith, diligence, and patience takes root and springs up unto everlasting life.

l: preaching of the word, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: The word of God is preached by Alma and others in synagogues, houses, and streets. It is also imparted by angels and given at times to men, women, and little children.

l: being cast out of the synagogues, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 32
s: Being cast out of the synagogues leaves the poor without a place to worship God and causes them to be despised because of their poverty. Their exclusion can bring them to humility and prepare them to hear the word.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: Alma teaches his listeners that they can worship God despite being cast out of their synagogues and urges them to search the scriptures. He cites Zenos, Zenock, Moses, and the type raised in the wilderness as witnesses of the Son of God and his mercy, atonement, resurrection, and judgment. Alma tells his listeners to plant the word in their hearts and nourish it by faith so it will become a tree leading to everlasting life and lighten their burdens through the joy of the Son of God.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: Alma teaches his listeners about worship, prayer, the scriptures, faith, and the Son of God. He urges them to plant the word in their hearts and nourish it by faith.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: God hears prayers and cries offered in the wilderness, fields, houses, closets, congregations, and afflictions. God is merciful to his children and can turn judgments away because of his Son.

l: Son of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: The Son of God is testified of by Zenos, Zenock, Moses, and the type raised in the wilderness. He will come to redeem his people, suffer and die to atone for their sins, rise from the dead, and judge all people.

l: Zenos, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: Zenos testified that God is merciful, hears prayer, and turns judgments away because of his Son.

l: Alma's listeners, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: Alma's listeners ask whether they should believe in one God, how to plant the seed or word in their hearts, and how to begin exercising faith. They had said they could not worship God because they were cast out of their synagogues.

l: holy scriptures, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: The scriptures teach about worship, prayer, the Son of God, and God's mercies. Alma asks his listeners whether they believe the scriptures written by those of old.

l: seed (Alma's listeners' seed), The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: The seed is identified with the word that Alma's listeners are to plant in their hearts. If nourished by faith, it will become a tree leading to everlasting life.

l: word of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: The word is to be planted in Alma's listeners' hearts and nourished by faith. It will become a tree and bring everlasting life.

l: faith in Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: Faith is used to plant and nourish the word in the heart. Alma tells his listeners to begin to believe in the Son of God.

l: prayer, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: Prayer is a form of turning to God that can be offered in the wilderness, field, house, closet, congregation, and affliction. God hears sincere prayers and cries.

l: worship at the holy stand, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: Alma's listeners mistakenly suppose that being cast out of their synagogues prevents them from worshiping God. Alma teaches that they can worship God and should search the scriptures.

l: mercy, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: God's mercy is shown by hearing prayers and cries and by turning judgments away because of his Son. Zenock testified that the people failed to understand God's mercies because of his Son.

l: sin, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: The Son of God will suffer and die to atone for the sins of his people.

l: type raised in the wilderness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: A type was raised in the wilderness so that whoever looked upon it might live. Many looked and lived, while those who would not look because they did not believe perished.

l: healing, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: Healing is presented as possible by looking upon the type raised in the wilderness. Alma asks whether people would look quickly if they could be healed merely by casting about their eyes.

l: the Atonement of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: The Son of God shall suffer and die to atone for the sins of his people.

l: resurrection of the dead, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: The Son of God shall rise again from the dead, which shall bring to pass the resurrection. All people shall stand before him afterward.

l: judgment day, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: At the last and judgment day, all people shall stand before the Son of God and be judged according to their works.

l: redemption of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: The Son of God will come to redeem his people.

l: tree (the planted word), The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: The planted word, when nourished by faith, will become a tree springing up in Alma's listeners unto everlasting life.

l: everlasting life, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 33
s: Everlasting life is the result of the word becoming a tree in Alma's listeners through faith and nourishment.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: Amulek teaches that Christ will come as the Son of God to atone for the sins of the world through an infinite and eternal sacrifice. He explains that mercy can satisfy the demands of justice for those who exercise faith unto repentance, while all mankind would otherwise perish. He exhorts the people to call upon God continually in prayer, care for the needy and afflicted, and bring forth fruit unto repentance. He teaches that this life is the time to prepare to meet God and warns that delaying repentance until death leads to the final state of the wicked.

l: Amulek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: Amulek teaches that Christ shall come among the children of men, take upon him the transgressions of his people, and atone for the sins of the world. He exhorts the people to exercise faith unto repentance, pray continually, care for those in need, and bear their afflictions with patience.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: Christ is taught as the Son of God who shall come to take upon him the transgressions of his people and atone for the sins of the world. His infinite and eternal sacrifice brings salvation to those who believe on his name.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: God has spoken that Christ shall come and atone for the sins of the world. He is mighty to save, grants mercy, and dwells in the hearts of the righteous.

l: Holy Ghost, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: The people are told not to contend against the Holy Ghost but to receive it. The Spirit of the Lord withdraws from those who procrastinate repentance until death.

l: devil, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: The devil is an enemy to all righteousness and may overpower those who are not watchful unto prayer. He possesses the bodies of those who procrastinate repentance until death and seals them as his subjects.

l: mankind, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: All mankind are hardened, fallen, and lost, and must perish except through the atonement. Mankind is given this life to prepare to meet God and perform its labors.

l: word of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: The word is taught as being in the Son of God unto salvation. The people are invited to plant the word in their hearts and try the experiment of its goodness.

l: faith in Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: Faith is to be exercised unto repentance and is necessary for the great and eternal plan of redemption. Those who have no faith unto repentance remain exposed to the whole law of the demands of justice.

l: afflictions, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: The people are exhorted to bear all manner of afflictions with patience and a firm hope that they shall one day rest from them. They are warned not to revile against those who cast them out because of their poverty.

l: the Atonement of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: An atonement is necessary because all mankind would otherwise unavoidably perish. Only an infinite atonement can suffice for the sins of the world.

l: redemption, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: The great plan of redemption is brought about for those who repent and do not harden their hearts. It is made possible through the infinite and eternal sacrifice of the Son of God.

l: salvation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: Salvation is brought to those who believe on the name of the Son of God. The people are told that now is the time and day of their salvation.

l: sacrifice, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: There must be a great and last sacrifice that is not a sacrifice of man, beast, or fowl. This sacrifice is the Son of God, and it fulfills the law of Moses.

l: mercy, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: Mercy brings about means for people to have faith unto repentance. It can satisfy the demands of justice and encircle those who exercise faith unto repentance in the arms of safety.

l: justice, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: Justice requires the life of the person who has murdered and exposes those without faith unto repentance to the whole law of its demands. Mercy can satisfy these demands for those who exercise faith unto repentance.

l: prayer, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: The people are commanded to call upon God for mercy and to cry unto him in their fields, houses, against their enemies and the devil, and over their crops and flocks. They are also told to pour out their souls in secret places and to keep their hearts drawn out in prayer continually.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: The people are urged to begin repentance immediately, harden not their hearts, and bring forth fruit unto repentance. Procrastinating repentance until death results in subjection to the spirit of the devil and the final state of the wicked.

l: the probationary state, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 34
s: This life is the time for people to prepare to meet God and perform their labors. If people do not improve their time in this life, the night of darkness comes when no labor can be performed.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 35
s: After Amulek finished speaking, Alma and his brethren came to the land of Jershon, where many Zoramites who favored their words had been cast out. The people of Ammon received the poor Zoramites, giving them food, clothing, lands, and help, which angered the Zoramites and led them to stir up the Lamanites against the people of Ammon and the Nephites. The people of Ammon moved to the land of Melek so Nephite armies could use Jershon, and war began between the Lamanites and the Nephites. Alma, Ammon, their brethren, and Alma's two sons returned to Zarahemla after bringing many Zoramites to repentance, while Alma grieved over the people's iniquity, wars, bloodshed, contentions, and hardening hearts.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 35
s: Alma and his brethren ministered to the Zoramites who came to the land of Jershon. Alma returned to Zarahemla after helping bring many Zoramites to repentance, and he was grieved by the iniquity, wars, bloodshed, contentions, and hardening hearts among the people.

l: Zoramites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 35
s: The Zoramites became angry because the word destroyed their craft and refused to hearken to it. They cast out those who favored the words of Alma and his brethren, stirred up the Lamanites against the people of Ammon and the Nephites, and prepared for war.

l: people of Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 35
s: The people of Ammon refused to cast out the Zoramites who came to them and instead received and supported the poor among them. They later departed from the land of Jershon and moved to the land of Melek to make room for the Nephite armies.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 35
s: The Lamanites were stirred up to anger by the Zoramites and began preparing for war against the people of Ammon and the Nephites.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 35
s: The Nephites prepared to contend with the armies of the Lamanites and the Zoramites. Their armies occupied the land of Jershon after the people of Ammon moved to the land of Melek.

l: land of Jershon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 35
s: The land of Jershon received Alma, Amulek, their brethren, and many Zoramites who had been cast out. The people of Ammon later gave place in the land of Jershon for the armies of the Nephites.

l: word of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 35
s: The word was preached to the Zoramites, but the more popular part became angry because it destroyed their craft and would not hearken. Some people favored the word, and their support led to their being cast out of the land.

l: preaching of the word, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 35
s: Alma and his brethren preached the word unto the Zoramites, and Alma had also declared or been sent to declare the word among the people in every city.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 35
s: Many Zoramites were brought to repentance through the efforts of Alma, Ammon, their brethren, and Alma's two sons. Those who repented were driven out of their land and received lands for their inheritance in the land of Jershon.

l: war preparations, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 35
s: War between the Lamanites and the Nephites commenced in the eighteenth year of the reign of the judges. The armies of the Nephites contended with the armies of the Lamanites and the Zoramites.

l: exile of the Zoramite believers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 35
s: Those who favored the words preached by Alma and his brethren were cast out of the land, and many came to the land of Jershon. The Zoramites who were brought to repentance were also driven out and received lands for their inheritance in Jershon.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 36
s: Alma teaches his son Helaman that keeping the commandments of God brings prosperity, while disobedience cuts people off from God’s presence. He recounts how God sent a holy angel to stop him and the sons of Mosiah from destroying the church of God, leading to Alma’s conversion. Alma describes suffering torment for his sins and iniquities, then receiving joy and relief through Jesus Christ. He says God has supported and delivered him and will raise him up at the last day.

l: Helaman, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 36
s: Helaman is Alma’s son. Alma teaches him to remember the captivity of their fathers, trust in God, and keep the commandments of God.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 36
s: God delivered the fathers from their afflictions and sent a holy angel to stop Alma and the sons of Mosiah. God supports those who trust in him, delivers them from bondage and captivity, and will raise them up at the last day.

l: Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 36
s: The fear of the Lord came upon Alma and the sons of Mosiah when the earth trembled and the angel spoke. Alma says the Lord gives him great joy through the fruit of his labors.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 36
s: Jesus Christ is identified as a Son of God who came to atone for the sins of the world. Alma called upon Jesus Christ for mercy and then remembered his pains no more.

l: sons of Mosiah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 36
s: The sons of Mosiah went with Alma seeking to destroy the church of God. A holy angel stopped them by the way.

l: church of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 36
s: Alma and the sons of Mosiah sought to destroy the church of God. The holy angel warned Alma to seek no more to destroy it.

l: holy angel, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 36
s: God sent a holy angel to stop Alma and the sons of Mosiah. The angel spoke with a voice like thunder and warned Alma to stop destroying the church of God.

l: fathers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 36
s: The fathers were in bondage, and God delivered them from their afflictions. Alma teaches Helaman to remember their captivity and says God brought them out of Egypt and the land of Jerusalem.

l: commandments of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 36
s: Those who keep the commandments of God will prosper in the land. Those who will not keep them will be cut off from God’s presence.

l: captivity, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 36
s: Alma remembers the captivity of the fathers and teaches Helaman to do the same. He says God has delivered them from captivity from time to time.

l: chains of hell, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 36
s: The fathers were in bondage, and none could deliver them except God. God has delivered people from bondage and captivity from time to time.

l: Alma's conversion, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 36
s: Alma’s conversion began when a holy angel stopped him and the sons of Mosiah from destroying the church of God. After suffering for three days and three nights, Alma called upon Jesus Christ, received joy and light, and was born of God.

l: sin, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 36
s: Alma remembered all his sins and iniquities and was tormented by them. He had rebelled against God, failed to keep his holy commandments, and led many of God’s children toward destruction.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 36
s: After his conversion, Alma labored without ceasing to bring souls unto repentance. He wanted them to taste the joy he had experienced and be born of God.

l: the Atonement of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 36
s: Alma remembered that Jesus Christ, a Son of God, would come to atone for the sins of the world. This thought led Alma to cry to Jesus Christ for mercy.
